$comment: The PC-01 journey, written down once and read by two checkers.
At RUN TIME `journey.mjs` walks these routes in order against a deployed origin, each
in its own cold browser process, and asserts that what the browser actually requested
matches `expects_api` here.
At GATE TIME `tests/e2e/test_pc01_journey_conformance.py` reads the same file with no
browser, no origin and no running stack, and asserts that every `page_module` exists,
that every screen in `web/src/app` is covered by exactly one route here, that the
dynamic segments of `path` match the `[param]` directories of `page_module`, and that
every (method, path, operationId) triple is a real operation in
`contracts/api/v1/openapi.json`.
That pairing is the anti-rot mechanism. Neither checker asks the application to
confirm itself: this file is an independent written claim, the gate checks it against
the route tree and the contract, and the journey checks it against live traffic.
`expects_api` paths are API paths -- the contract's own paths, WITHOUT the `/bff/v1`
prefix the browser adds. Query strings are not declared and not matched: `?limit=50`
is a pagination choice, not a seam.
The SIGN-IN. `D-92`, repaired by `W44-JOURNEY` 2026-09-24.
The BFF answers `401` without a session cookie -- wave 34, by design -- and this
journey was written for the application as it stood before that. It walked two routes
of fifteen for nine waves, and a shorter walk looked like a walk.
At RUN TIME `session.mjs` opens ONE cold browser at the address below, fills the two
fields through the browser's own editing pipeline, presses the control by its own
label, and carries the single `HttpOnly` cookie the exchange sets into every later
cold browser -- identically, as a value, never as a shared jar. Each route therefore
begins from an empty profile plus exactly one stated cookie, which `journey.mjs`
reads back per route before it navigates. `D-16`'s cold-load property is measured
rather than assumed.
THERE IS NO CREDENTIAL HERE AND THERE MAY NEVER BE ONE. Each `fill` names the FIELD
it fills -- `from`: `login` or `password` -- and the value comes from
`E2E_PC01_LOGIN` / `E2E_PC01_PASSWORD` at run time, with no default and no file.
`tests/e2e/test_pc01_journey_conformance.py` refuses a session action carrying a
literal `value`, so the gate is what keeps a password out of this repository rather
than this paragraph.

api.$why: the exchange is this tier's own and is never forwarded: the browser receives a 303 and an opaque cookie, and the minted credential never crosses the network. See web/src/app/bff/v1/[...path]/route.ts.

$comment: The declared width every route is laid out at. `D-93`, `W44-JOURNEY` 2026-09-24.
Wave 43 added four navigation links, `.am-app__bar` stopped fitting, and the overflow
threshold moved from 482 px to 839 px -- so every screen in the product carried a
horizontal scrollbar on a small laptop and on every tablet. 1085 frontend tests could
not see it: the battery renders through `renderToStaticMarkup`, which has no layout,
no box and no viewport. A judge driving a browser found it.
780 is the width `W43-JUDGE-B` measured the regression at, and is deliberately the
SAME number, so this assertion and that finding are comparable. It sits between the
old threshold (482) and the new one (839), which is what makes it able to see the
class: a bar that fits at 839 passes here, a bar that does not fails here.
The verdict is `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= window.innerWidth`, per route,
after the page has settled. `innerWidth` rather than `clientWidth` on purpose: a
vertical scrollbar makes `clientWidth` smaller than the viewport, and a page exactly
filling the viewport would then redden for a scrollbar rather than for a layout. The
looser of the two comparisons is the one that cannot produce a false red.
Shown failing by `prove_the_width_assertion_can_fail.mjs`, which restores the
`flex-wrap` this bar had before wave 43 repaired it and requires this assertion to
redden.

unlike W38-KB, which had it in its forbidden_hotspots and correctly stopped.
`expects_api` is EMPTY and that is the claim, not an omission -- the same claim the

and not a contract path. The contract operation it reaches -- changePassword, POST
/auth/password -- is called by the NODE process, never by the browser: the whole
`auth` segment is refused to a browser precisely because that operation answers with
a credential, and a credential in a page body is what JUDGE-SEC drove out of
issueToken.
So a declared call here would be false in the way this manifest is least able to
tolerate: the run-time walk asserts what the BROWSER requested, and the browser
requests nothing of the API on this screen.
`follow: null` -- it captures no identity a later step needs, and it is deliberately
not the last thing the write half does: succeeding here revokes every credential the
account holds, so a journey that changed the password mid-walk would be walking with
a dead one.

$comment: The WRITE half of the journey. `D-30`, and before it `D-5`.
`D-5` was `POST /api/v1/runs` -> 500, twice, through a browser, on 2026-09-16. The
read walk above would not have caught it: it makes no POST. These three steps do what
a user does -- name a project and press Create, choose the portal bundle (a ZIP) and press Upload,
press Start run -- through the app's own controls, on the public origin.
Read by the same two checkers as `routes`. At RUN TIME `write.mjs` presses these
controls and asserts the request, the status, the response body and what the screen
rendered afterwards. At GATE TIME the conformance guard asserts that every
`page_module` and `control_module` exists, that each step's `at` is a route the read
walk also covers, that every (method, path, operationId) triple is a real contract
operation, that the fixture is on disk, and that every selector, text and marker
attribute named here still appears in `web/src`.
That last check is new. `W21-E2E` stated the guard's cost as 'it checks addressing,
not behaviour'. The write half's handles are not addressing, so leaving them unguarded
would have meant a renamed id turns the journey red only when someone runs it. The
check is still not behaviour -- it proves the handle exists in the source, not that
pressing it does anything -- and that residue is stated rather than closed.
`%STAMP%` is replaced with the run's UTC timestamp. The app mints its idempotency key
from the typed name, so a fixed name would make every run the same command and the
second run of the day would assert nothing about creation.
BETA-LIVE-JOURNEY-01. After the first four steps (project, upload, classify, run) come the
steps for the screens the night window of 2026-10-20 added -- the next version of a set,
the version and П→Р comparisons and the carried decision, «Нормы», «Настройки анализа»,
«Диспетчер» and «Мои задачи», the project's «Оптимизация» tab (price list, vendor lists,
«Спецификация и цены», «Предложения») and «Оптимизация разделов» -- each with the case
that must be refused: a role the screen refuses, an input it refuses, or a second identical
submit that must change nothing. `as` names the session that performs a step (`admin` is the
journey's own account, holding both roles; the others are the `accounts` roster). `bind`
renames what a template variable means inside a step, so a step that works on the set's
second version still names its route and its contract path the way they are written.
`on_red: continue_if_captured` stops only the steps whose inputs a red step failed to
produce; a step that was not reached is a finding, never a pass.
PROD-10B-JOURNEY-REBASE-01. This half runs on section ПБ (see `classify-version`) EXCEPT the steps named
here, which cannot: the project's «Оптимизация» tab -- price lists, vendor lists, «Спецификация и цены»,
optimisation passes and proposals -- and the Form-7 of the АР section exist for АР only (a set of another
section is answered `section_not_ar`), and the specification and the passes read the saved page text of
the newest PUBLISHED run of an АР version. That run used to be an АР v1 run started with «Запустить прогон».
PROD-11-AR-V1-V2-REMOVAL-01 removed it: `startRun` refuses an АР version (`section_profile_unavailable`),
an АР version can start only the v3 group, and that group needs an installed reviewed pack (`D-204`) and,
in recorded mode, a provider binding with a verifiable cost (`D-225` piece 2) before it publishes. Until
a published АР run can exist, every step of `steps` carries `pending_v3_activation: true`: the driver
(`write.mjs`) does NOT run it, prints `PENDING <step> ... NOT RUN: <reason>` for each, counts it as
pending and not as checked, and ends `OK WITH PENDING` and never plain `OK`; `verify-acceptance.mjs`
refuses an envelope with pending steps. Nothing is deleted: removing the mark is how a step is
reactivated, and `tests/e2e/test_pc01_journey_section.py` refuses an АР classification, an АР pin or a
run start on an АР version anywhere else in this half, a listed step without the mark and a marked step
that is not listed.
`steps` is every step that may name АР. `needs_published_run` is the subset that cannot pass without a
published АР run, directly or through the pass it produced (read from the steps' own expectations, not
measured). `registry_pins` name the АР ROW of the profile registry, which has no profile now (the row
reads `data-profile="none"`, `data-profile-absent="ar-v3"`); that step still runs.
ar_bound.pending_v3_activation_reason: no published АР run can exist: startRun refuses АР (section_profile_unavailable) and the six-run АР v3 group needs an installed reviewed pack (D-204)

$comment: The run reaches its terminal asynchronously. This does NOT sleep: it reads

steps.no_negative_case: a read-only panel: it takes no input and offers no control, and every role that can open the dashboard reads the same counts; its refusal (an incomplete breakdown) is `data-panel-fault`, forbidden above

steps.name: blocks-portal-blocks-of-a-version-with-a-run
$comment: PC01-JOURNEY-GAPS-01. «Блоки»: choose the project, then the document, whose current version is the third
version of the baseline set (its run has published, so a run reached the page geometry). The rows of the
chooser carry no handle, so each choice is the button of the row whose words name the project (the name the
journey gave it) and then the version (its identity is printed in the row).
«Блоки портала» is the tab it opens on: the committed bundle holds twelve blocks (eight text, two stamp, two
image), the API lists them, and each image block carries a crop the application cut from the PDF. The crop is
loaded lazily by the browser, so the step scrolls the first image into view by pressing it (a press on a
picture does nothing) and reads the crop's address from the picture itself.

captures.$why: the crop's address names the block; the crop call is declared with it

steps.name: blocks-text-lines-of-the-same-version
$comment: The second tab, «Строки текста»: the text-line index of the same version (`getVersionBlocks`). Each line is
listed with its page, its bounds in points and its character span; nothing is computed by the screen.

steps.name: classification-correction-is-an-experts-act
$comment: PC01-JOURNEY-GAPS-01. A role the screen refuses. The first version's classification is confirmed (stage П,
section ПБ). An administrator without `expert` reads it and its history and is offered no «Исправить»: the API
refuses a correction to `admin` alone, and the panel draws no control for it.

expects_not_called.why: an administrator without `expert` is offered no correction

steps.name: classification-correction-needs-a-change
$comment: An input the form refuses: a reason with nothing changed. The form opens on the current stage and section, so
a good reason beside the same pair is still no correction -- the form says the pair matches the current one and
holds the button. Nothing is sent.

actions.value: Причина есть, но стадия и раздел те же

expects_present.text_contains: Стадия и раздел совпадают с текущими.

expects_not_called.why: a pair equal to the current one is no correction

steps.name: classification-correction-needs-a-reason
$comment: An input the form refuses: a changed stage with no reason in words. Punctuation alone has no letter or digit,
so the form says a reason is needed and holds the button; nothing is sent.

expects_not_called.why: a reason with no letter or digit is no reason

steps.name: classification-correction
$comment: `correctVersionClassification`. The expert corrects the first version's stage from П to Р, keeping the section
ПБ, with a reason, pressing the button twice: one request, based on revision 1, and revision 2 is stored. The
panel closes the form and says the classification was corrected, and the history keeps the original
confirmation beside the correction with its reason.
Only the stage changes, and only on the first version: a change of section would move the project out of the
ПБ figures the steps before it counted, and a later version's stage is what the comparisons read.

steps.name: queue-pause-dispatch
$comment: W53/W54 execution controls. The administrator pauses the issue of jobs (a confirmation first); the
queue says so, and the button becomes «Возобновить выдачу».

steps.name: queue-start-a-run-while-paused
$comment: With dispatch paused a run is accepted and waits: it is queued and no worker takes it.

steps.name: queue-lists-the-waiting-run
$comment: The waiting run is in the queue, ahead of the finished ones. An expert may cancel it and is offered neither the
priority field nor the pause: those are an administrator's.

captures.$why: the job's identity, printed as words; the priority command's address carries it

steps.name: queue-priority-out-of-range-refused
$comment: An input the field refuses: a priority of 500 (the range is -100..100). Nothing is sent.

expects_not_called.why: 500 is outside -100..100

steps.name: queue-change-priority
$comment: The administrator raises the waiting job's priority to 7 (confirmation first); the row says so.

steps.name: queue-cancel-the-waiting-run
$comment: An expert cancels the waiting run (confirmation first). The row now offers a re-audit instead.

steps.name: queue-reaudit-the-cancelled-run
$comment: A re-audit of the cancelled run starts a new run of the same version (accepted, 202); the queue links to it.

steps.name: queue-resume-dispatch
$comment: Dispatch resumes (confirmation first); the paused notice goes and the waiting re-audit is taken by a worker.

steps.name: workers-list-the-worker
$comment: Исполнители. The lane runs one worker beside the API (EXECUTION_ROLE=worker); it is registered, active and takes new work.

captures.$why: the active worker's identity, printed as words

steps.name: worker-intake-is-an-administrators-act
$comment: An expert reads the workers and is offered no switch.

steps.name: worker-stops-taking-new-work
$comment: The administrator stops the worker taking new jobs (confirmation first); its row says intake is off.

steps.name: worker-takes-new-work-again
$comment: And allows it again, so the lane's runs are taken.

steps.name: profile-needs-a-surname
$comment: Профиль. An input the form refuses: the surname is required. Cleared, the save button sends nothing.

expects_not_called.why: a profile without a surname

steps.name: profile-update
$comment: The account's own names are saved (here the patronymic); the screen says so.

steps.name: password-confirmation-must-match
$comment: Сменить пароль. A new password and a repeat that differ are refused by the web tier: it redirects with
`outcome=mismatch` and sends nothing on to the accounts service. (The account is the administrator-only
one: changing a password ends the passes issued under the old one, and the expert's session is still needed.)

expects_not_called.why: the tier refuses a mismatch before the API

steps.name: password-current-must-be-right
$comment: The wrong current password changes nothing: `outcome=credentials`, no pass is revoked.

steps.name: password-change
$comment: The password is changed. Every pass issued under the old one is revoked and THIS browser continues on a new
one: the same browser opens the profile afterwards.

steps.name: old-pass-is-refused-after-the-password-change
$comment: Everything issued under the old password stopped being accepted at once: the cookie this account signed in
with opens nothing, and the browser is sent to sign in.

expects_not_called.why: the pass was revoked

steps.name: user-password-reset-must-match
$comment: Пользователи. An input the form refuses: a temporary password and its repeat that differ. Nothing is sent.

expects_not_called.why: the repeat differs

steps.name: user-archive
$comment: The administrator archives the administrator-only account (confirmation first); the card says archived.

steps.name: user-restore
$comment: And restores it; the card says active again.

steps.name: user-password-reset
$comment: The administrator sets a temporary password for the account (it must be changed at the next sign-in). The
value is typed and never recorded; the screen says it was reset.

steps.name: release-history-panel
$comment: История версий, from the account menu: a dialog with what changed in each release.
steps.no_negative_case: the history is read by every complete account whose password is not the shipped one; an account that is not complete cannot be made without leaving it for good, and the API answers the read for any role

steps.name: sign-out
$comment: Выйти, from the account menu: a POST to the tier's own door; the answer is a redirect to the sign-in screen.

steps.name: signed-out-session-is-gone
$comment: The pass that was just closed opens nothing: the same cookie, a protected screen, and the browser is sent to sign in.

expects_not_called.why: the session no longer exists

$comment: BETA-LIVE-JOURNEY-01. The accounts a refusal by role needs, made the way a person gets one:
the applicant fills the registration form in a cold browser, the journey's administrator
approves the request choosing the roles, the applicant signs in (`accounts.mjs`).
The journey's own account holds BOTH roles (the seeded administrator is also an expert), so
as that account no control is ever refused for a missing role. `expert_only` is refused what
is an administrator's -- assigning work, the global vendor list -- and `admin_only` is
refused what is an expert's -- confirming a section, starting a pass, carrying a decision.
The screens draw no control for the role that cannot use it, and the API refuses the
request anyway; the steps check the first, the integration suites check the second.
No password is declared here or anywhere in this repository: each is random per run, typed
into the form, used for one sign-in and never written to the envelope or to stdout.
W51 Stage C. identity.mjs drives these operations through the browser. It consumes
the run written by the PC-01 write half, and the administrator credential from
E2E_PC01_LOGIN/PASSWORD. Its generated applicant passwords are never recorded.
The BFF session register path is supplied at run time, never committed; a 401
without a before/after row reading is not accepted as proof of session deletion.
The REFUSAL half. `D-44`, and before it `W27-REFUSE`'s six drives.
`W55B-INGEST-01`: the upload takes a portal bundle (a ZIP) and a bare PDF is refused, so
the six are now: three refused by the BROWSER before any byte is sent (a bare PDF, a
text file, and a sparse file past 250 MiB) and three refused by the SERVER with a
constraint the screen states in Russian (an encrypted PDF, an image-only PDF, 501
pages). A bare PDF is refused by the browser here; the server's own refusal of one
(`portal_bundle_required`) is covered by a server-side test, because no screen can send
it. Two of the six files are GENERATED when the drive starts (`generated`, below):
250 MiB is too large to commit and 501 pages exist only to sit one past the limit.
`routes` and `write` both declare steps that SUCCEED. These six declare what happens
when a person drops the wrong file into the upload control: where the refusal happened,
what the screen said, and that the screen named the specific rule rather than a generic
failure. `W27-REFUSE` drove all six through a browser on 2026-09-18 and all six held --
and wrote the verdicts into `refusals.mjs`'s own source, where `make gate` cannot see
them. That is what moving them here fixes.
Read by the same two checkers as the other halves. At RUN TIME `refusals.mjs` attaches
each fixture at the app's own control and asserts every field below against what the
browser saw. At GATE TIME the conformance guard asserts, with no stack: the fixture is
on disk; `refused_by` is `client` or `server` and the case declares the fields that go
with it and none that do not; the operation triple is a real contract operation and the
declared status is one the contract publishes FOR THAT OPERATION -- a `422` is as
declarable as a `201`; every marker attribute and every marker VALUE named here still
appears in `web/src`; every sentence in `expects_rendered` still appears in `web/src`;
and no case declares a classification from `generic_kinds`.
WHICH HALF DOES NOT MOVE, stated rather than quietly widened. The gate cannot see that
the envelope really carries that `constraint`, that the screen really renders it, that
`Upload` really goes unpressable, or that nothing was published. Those are behaviour and
they stay with `refusals.mjs` against a running stack. `expects_rendered_from_envelope`
is the part of the rendered text the SERVER supplies, so it is deliberately not checked
against `web/src` -- it is checked against the `constraint` beside it instead, which is
data and therefore guardable.
`fixture` is relative to the case's own `fixture_dir` when it names one, else to the section's; a case
with `generated: true` is found in the temporary directory the tool filled instead.
Two of the six files are not committed. A case that says `"generated": true` has its file in a
temporary directory that `refusals.mjs` fills, by running `tool`, before the first drive and
deletes after the last. `files` is the set the tool writes (`--list` prints the same names
and the conformance guard holds the two equal); a sparse file is never allocated on disk.

api.$why: the one call a server-side refusal makes. A client-side refusal makes none, which is half of what these cases assert.

$comment: The controls the six drives press and read. `W44-JOURNEY` 2026-09-24, and the
reason they are here is `W28-GUARD`'s reason applied to the half it did not move.
They were literals in `refusals.mjs`'s own source -- `Create`, `Upload`, `Retry`,
`Chosen: ` -- and the gate cannot read that file. The application was translated
and every one of them stopped matching: MEASURED 2026-09-24, `refusals.mjs` threw
`click form button[type="submit"] [text="Create"]: no element matches it` before it
drove a single fixture. So `D-83`'s "outside the gate `refusals.mjs` drives them
against a live stand" was not true either: the eleven sentences were verified by
nothing at all, in the gate or out of it.
Declared here, they are handles like any other and
`test_every_control_the_refusals_press_still_exists_in_the_application` reddens
`make gate` the next time one is relabelled.
The retry action is read by CLASS because `.am-state__action` is structure
shared/ui owns whatever the action says. The chosen-file line is found by class
and its visible prefix is asserted from `chosen_label`, so translating it cannot
silently leave the live refusal drive green over stale prose.

cases.$why_a_bare_pdf_is_client_side: The committed baseline PDF is exactly what a person holds before they have a bundle. The browser refuses it before sending, so the server's own refusal (`portal_bundle_required`, a bare PDF that reaches the route) is covered by tests/integration/api/test_multipart_rules.py through the HTTP route, not by this screen. `Отдельный PDF не принимается` is NOT declared here: the upload panel prints it before any file is chosen, so it could not fail (D-61).

cases.$why_the_size_case_is_client_side: `D-44`. It is client-side only while the pre-check limit stays strictly below nginx's `client_max_body_size`; tests/e2e/test_upload_limit_headroom.py is what keeps that true. The file is a sparse 251 MiB stand-in with a ZIP's first bytes, generated into a temporary directory when the drive starts; the pre-check reads its size and its name, so not one byte of it is read or sent.
cases.$why_not_the_limit: D-61, W41-BLIND 2026-09-23. This case declared the limit as well, and the upload panel prints `Не более 250 MiB на архив.` before any file is chosen -- so that half of the assertion was satisfied by the envelope notice on an untouched screen. `Ничего не отправлено` is rendered only by the pre-check refusal panel and is the half that is evidence.
cases.$why_the_rule_specific_half_is_back: W44-JOURNEY 2026-09-24. `Этот файл больше, чем` is authored in entities/document-version/model/upload-envelope.ts and rendered by the too_large pre-check and by nothing else. The size itself is interpolated, so the sentence stops where the template does -- declaring the number back would be declaring a value the source does not author.

Число страниц PDF вне допустимых границ
cases.$why_it_is_generated: 501 pages is the smallest document past the limit; it exists to sit one past it and is built into a temporary directory when the drive starts (tools/fixtures/build_journey_inputs.py).
